entry.title: The Limitations of the 'Next-Token Predictor' Model for LLMs
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | gmcgoldr.github.io | discussion | hacker news

The 'next-token predictor' label for Large Language Models (LLMs) is technically accurate regarding the autoregressive mechanism but incomplete as a conceptual model. Pre-training involves predicting tokens found in existing training data, whereas Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) allows models to explore and learn from new, non-sequential outcomes.

This shift is analogous to a chess engine that transitions from mimicking grandmaster moves to optimizing for winning probability through exploration. Consequently, the mechanism can encode complex behaviors and discovered knowledge rather than just statistical patterns from existing text.

TechCrunch AI | techcrunch.com | source

Alexa for Shopping can now identify whether a text, email, or phone call is an authentic communication from the retailer. The AI analyzes metadata, timing, and content, comparing suspicious messages against a global database of billions of legitimate Amazon communications to provide a definitive answer regarding the sender's identity.

The feature aims to reduce the high volume of customer service inquiries caused by potential scams, which currently reach Amazon's support teams roughly 360,000 times per year. This update is part of a broader effort to pivot Alexa's capabilities toward proactive shopping assistance and security features.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is an iteration of the Gemini 3 model family, optimized for software engineering and agentic knowledge workflows. It supports multimodal inputs, including text, images, audio, and video, with a context window of up to 1 million tokens and a 64,000 token output limit.

The model supports customizable effort levels to manage the balance between quality, cost, and latency. While improvements were noted in text-to-text safety and tone, the model showed slight regressions in multilingual safety and unjustified refusal rates compared to Gemini 3.7 Flash.

entry.title: Neural Network Representations Implicitly Realize Symbolic Structure
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | arxiv.org | hacker news

Neural network internal representations implicitly implement symbolic structures, even though the models operate within continuous vector spaces. Using a method called DISCOVER, researchers approximated the representations of both small-scale networks and large language models (LLMs) using closed-form symbolic equations in domains such as arithmetic, logic, code, and language.

These symbolic approximations enable targeted interventions on LLMs, allowing for the precise modification of model behavior via internal representations. This research provides a potential framework for reconciling traditional symbolic intelligence theories with the vector-based nature of modern artificial intelligence.
